I'm gonna write a bit about Alice Pleasance Liddell and her relationship to Alice in Wonderland if anyone is interested.

As can be inferred from the article, Carroll loves children. He was particularly close to the three Liddell sisters, and AIW originated from the stories he told to them on a boat trip across the river Thames.

In fact, he loved children so much that his greatest fear was of them growing up and maturing into the adults which he so hated for their logical ways. He preferred the whimsical, a key facet of youth, and thus, Alice in Wonderland.

He closes off Through the Looking Glass with this poem: http://m.poemhunter.com/poem/epilogue-to-through-the-looking-glass/

It's an acrostic, with the first letters of each sentence spelling out Alice Pleasance Liddell. He immortalized her youth by writing us AIW.

To give a somewhat basic analysis of the poem:

A boat, beneath a sunny sky

Lingering onward dreamily

In an evening of July --

Children three that nestle near,

Eager eye and willing ear

Pleased a simple tale to hear --

The first stanza refers to the boat trip where the story was first created, and 'The Children Theee that nestle near' represent the three Liddell sisters.

Long has paled that sunny sky:

Echoes fade and memories die:

Autumn frosts have slain July.

Still she haunts me, phantomwise

Alice moving under skies

Never seen by waking eyes.

This suggests that the author (Carroll) is already dead, but Alice continues to live.

In a Wonderland they lie,

Dreaming as the days go by,

Dreaming as the summers die:

Ever drifting down the stream --

The children he love lie in Wonderland, a place where he created so that time never pasts, so that it's always teatime, so that it is always filled with a child's whimsy no matter how fast they drift down the stream of time, where he can keep the children he so loved forever young.

TL;DR: Lewis Carroll loved children so much that he created Wonderland as a place where they would never die. His Alice in Wonderland is also a gigantic tribute to Alice, the child he loved most of all, and a successful bid to immortalize her from death.
